label: Pixel art (16-bit retro game)
summary: Crisp 16-bit pixel art with a limited palette, side-scrolling and top-down game framings, stepped animation and dithered light.
look: Crisp 16-bit pixel art like a polished retro console game. Every element is drawn with hard-edged square pixels on a low-resolution grid, a limited 32-colour palette, ordered dithering for gradients and lighting, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no photographic texture. Clear readable silhouettes, parallax background layers, bold saturated colours.
character_medium: one original pixel-art character drawn as a crisp 16-bit sprite with a limited 32-colour palette, clear silhouette, no anti-aliasing, game-hero proportions
sheet_backdrop: Flat solid dark background, sprites evenly spaced, no text.
plate_medium: a 16-bit pixel-art game background scene with parallax layers, empty of characters
motion: Stepped sprite animation at about 12 frames per second, like a retro game: walk cycles, snappy poses, hard cuts between poses, parallax scrolling backgrounds, no motion blur, no smooth interpolation, the pixel grid never warps.
constraints: No photorealism, no smooth gradients, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no 3D rendering, no readable text, no logos.
critic: pixels stay square and crisp (no smearing or soft edges)
palette stays limited, no photographic gradients
